minutes.headline: Personnel Committee heard the HR consultant's draft pay plan and agreed to add a Feb 27 pop-up meeting before the mid-March deadline.
minutes.summary: The HR consultant gave an update on the classification and compensation study: job description template, midpoint differentials, and a conservative draft pay plan with possible letter grades. The committee discussed how to deliver the job descriptions and how to schedule review ahead of the mid-March finance deadline. January minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none heard at opening.
A speaker said the finance presentation schedule does not list the Personnel committee and suggested the consultant warn Heather of a potential increase.

votes.outcome: passed (ayes heard from members; no dissent)

budget_items.topic: Proposed pay plan grade 2 starting rate
budget_items.what_was_said: Consultant proposed eliminating grade one and starting grade two near minimum wage to stay competitive.
Draft uses a uniform increase between grades and steps, with a small step increment as industry standard to stay under the Prop 2.5 cap.
Consultant said the plan is intentionally conservative to avoid a costly product.
Members said the impact must be known for the FY24 budget and the mid-March deadline for town meeting warrant/finance.

decisions.decision: Hold a pop-up meeting on February 27 in addition to the regular March 6 meeting, after the final report arrives.
Job descriptions will be shared via Dropbox rather than embedded in the report.
Consultant to send copies of the slides to the committee.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee agreed to hold an extra meeting on February 27, in addition to the regular March 6 meeting, once the consultant's final report arrives.
The HR consultant presented a draft pay plan for the classification and compensation study, described as intentionally conservative, with possible letter grades.
The draft pay plan would drop grade one and start grade two near minimum wage, with small, uniform step increments meant to stay under the Prop 2.5 cap.
Job descriptions will be shared with the committee through Dropbox rather than embedded in the report, and the consultant will send copies of the slides.
Members said the pay plan's effect on the FY24 budget must be known before the mid-March deadline for the town meeting warrant and finance review.

why_it_matters: The pay plan that comes out of this study sets the wage scale for town employees, so its cost will reach the FY24 budget and, through it, the tax levy residents vote on at town meeting.
The mid-March deadline and the extra February 27 meeting leave little time for public review of a pay plan before the warrant is set.
watch_next: February 27 pop-up Personnel Committee meeting, after the consultant's final report arrives.
Regular Personnel Committee meeting on March 6, ahead of the mid-March finance and warrant deadline.
